title: The soul of the fast
hook: the fast is a shield, so don't shout or quarrel (Bukhari)

segments.voice: Yesterday, fidyah, and your line: feed instead. Those who can never fast feed someone for each day. Did you find something you could still give? Day one thousand one hundred ten.

Five in the evening, the last hour of a long fasting day. Blood sugar is low, traffic is worse, and someone cuts in line at the store. Every part of the body wants to say something sharp. These past days have been about the rules: the intention, what breaks the fast, who is excused, how days are made up. All of it about the stomach. But the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ said something about the fast that has nothing to do with food, and everything to do with that moment in the line. Today, the soul of the fast.
screen: `THE LAST HOUR, A LONG LINE.` → `THE RULES WERE ABOUT FOOD.` → `THIS IS ABOUT THE TONGUE.`

segments.voice: First, the image. In a report in Sahih al-Bukhari the Prophet ﷺ says the fast is a junnah, a shield. A shield is held up between you and something that would hurt you. In that same report, he says what the shield is for: when one of you is fasting, don't speak obscenely and don't shout. And if someone insults you or picks a fight, say: I am fasting. Not a comeback. A reminder, as much to yourself as to them. Second, without this, the fast can go hollow. Another report in Bukhari is blunt: whoever doesn't give up lying and acting on lies, Allah has no need of them giving up their food and drink. An empty stomach and a sharp tongue, in this report, don't add up to a fast. Third, it connects to the purpose the Qur'an gave on the first day of this part. Surah two said the fast is prescribed so that, in Pickthall's words, "ye may ward off (evil)." The shield and the warding off are close pictures. In this reading, hunger is the training, and what's being guarded is what comes out of a person when they're tired and provoked. Fourth, the same report in Bukhari carries a saying from Allah, a hadith qudsi: every deed of a person is for them, except fasting, which is for Allah, and Allah rewards it. Some teachers say that's because no one else can see a fast. A secret kept between a person and Allah, and the proof of it shows in how they treat the person in front of them. Fasting or not, the shield works the same way: one sentence, said quietly, before the sharp one.
screen: `JUNNAH: THE FAST IS A SHIELD.` · `SAY: I AM FASTING.` · `NO LIES, OR THE FAST IS HOLLOW.` · `A SECRET BETWEEN A PERSON AND ALLAH.` · then, large: `THAT YE MAY WARD OFF (EVIL).`

segments.voice: The practice: keep calm all day, and rehearse it now. Settle, and breathe. Picture the place where your temper is most likely to slip today: a meeting, a commute, a sibling, a comment section. See it coming. Then choose your shield sentence. If you're fasting, it can be the Prophet's: I am fasting. If you're not, any short line that reminds you who you mean to be. Say it silently on each out-breath, until it feels ready in your mouth. If you pray, you can ask Allah for patience. The bell holds the time.
The soul of the fast. The fast as a shield: no shouting, no quarreling, no lies; and when provoked, I am fasting. Today's word.
screen: `THE SOUL OF THE FAST — today's word`.

segments.voice: Your line: a shield. Today, when something sharp rises in you, say your shield sentence first, silently, and then decide. Day one thousand one hundred ten.

howItsDone: Muslims who are fasting try to guard their speech and temper as well as their stomachs, and when provoked some say, as the Prophet taught, "I am fasting."

fork.setup: it's the last hour of your fast, and someone insults you to your face. what does the report in Bukhari say to do?
options: stay silent and walk away without a word.
answer back, but keep it polite.
fork.reveal: say: I am fasting. the fast is a shield, and the shield is a sentence.

original.note: Arabic: a shield, a covering; the Prophet's word for the fast.

trapdoor: what you thought: fasting is about not eating.
what it means: it's also a shield: no shouting, no quarrels, no lies.
what a scholar hears: as-siyamu junnah, in the same Bukhari report as the hadith qudsi 'fasting is for Me'.

notes: Bukhari 1904 (fasting is a shield; no obscenity or shouting; say 'I am fasting'; hadith qudsi 'fasting is for Me'): confirm number, that these are in one report. Some wordings repeat 'I am fasting' twice; left out under the claims rule.
Bukhari 1903 (whoever does not give up false speech and acting on it): confirm number and paraphrase.
Pickthall 2:183 phrase quoted from memory; confirm.
'Some teachers say' the fast is for Allah because it is unseen: attributed reading; confirm.
'I am fasting' is spoken as a reported instruction, not a new prayer; the practice offers a personal reminder line for non-fasters without writing one.
Editor pass: the narrator's own claim about what the fast guards is now framed as a reading; stock 'ordinary Tuesday' turn replaced.
